lead: EDM measures a distance by sending an electromagnetic wave to a target and comparing either travel time or phase with the returning wave. Tape is slow and unsafe over long or busy ground; EDM gives a fast electronic reading that is stored and processed. Surveyors use it for control, setting out, boundaries, roads and construction. Accuracy is quoted as a constant part plus a part per million of the distance, so long lines have larger uncertainty.
prereq: You need: measurements, errors, accuracy and precision and chain and tape surveying.

blocks.text: An electromagnetic wave travels through air at speed v, close to 3×10⁸ m/s. A pulse EDM sends a short burst, starts a clock, receives the echo and measures total travel time Δt. The one-way distance is half the path length.

blocks.where: d is the one-way distance in m; v is the wave speed in air in m/s; Δt is the total there-and-back travel time in s.

blocks.text: Most survey EDM uses phase difference. The transmitter sends a continuous wave modulated at frequency f. The returning wave has phase lag Δφ. The instrument measures only the fractional cycle. It repeats at several frequencies to find N, the whole number of cycles.

blocks.where: d is the one-way distance; λ = v/f is the modulation wavelength in air; N is the whole number of cycles in the double path; Δφ is the phase difference in radians.

blocks.text: λ = v/f is the modulation wavelength in air. Fine frequency gives resolution; coarse frequency gives the metre range. One frequency alone cannot give an unambiguous long distance. Pulse and phase both need the wave speed in air, so atmospheric correction applies to both.

EDM instruments are also grouped by the carrier wave. Microwave instruments carry the signal on radio waves; they reach tens of kilometres and need a second active unit at the far end, not a prism. Electro-optical instruments use infrared or visible light returned by a glass prism; almost all total stations are of this kind. A laser carrier also lets the instrument measure without a prism, from the faint diffuse return of a wall or rock.

Typical prism EDM range is a few hundred metres to several kilometres. Reflectorless EDM reflects from the object surface and works from a few metres to a few hundred metres; range depends on colour and roughness. Display resolution is often 1 mm or 0.1 mm; resolution is not accuracy.

blocks.where: σ<sub>d</sub> is the expected error in mm; a is the constant part in mm; b is the distance-dependent part in ppm; d is the measured distance in km.

blocks.text: The constant part covers instrument zero error and phase resolution. Centring adds a separate field error. The ppm part covers atmospheric and frequency uncertainty. For ±(3 mm + 3 ppm), at 1 km the ppm part is 3 mm; the total is 6 mm.

items: Prism: a retroreflector returns the beam parallel; its prism constant is a small offset, such as 0 or −30 mm, entered in the instrument.
Tribrach: levels and centres the instrument over the station with an optical plummet.
Thermometer and barometer: give temperature and pressure for atmospheric correction.
Target plate: helps aim in reflectorless mode.
EDM without a prism: uses diffuse reflection; no prism constant, shorter range, surface-dependent accuracy.

blocks.text: Operation: set the instrument on the station with a tribrach and level it; set the prism on the target station; enter prism constant, temperature and pressure; aim at the prism; press measure; record slope distance. Reduce the slope distance S to horizontal with the vertical angle α read at the same time: horizontal distance = S cos α. A total station is EDM plus electronic angle measurement; its parts and errors are taught with the total station in modern surveying.

Prism constant error: a wrong constant shifts every distance by the same amount. Atmospheric error: wave speed depends on air density, so temperature and pressure mistakes produce ppm errors. Cyclic error: a small periodic error with phase, often a few millimetres, from signal leakage. Centring error: instrument or target not over the mark; random, and larger in effect on short lines. Frequency error and resolution also contribute.

The worked example below combines the constant and ppm parts. In field practice, record temperature and pressure at the instrument, not hours later. Check the prism constant whenever the prism type changes; a 30 mm mistake is impossible to miss on a short line but easy to blame on the instrument.

figure.caption: The fine frequency measures only the last part of a 10 m unit (3.07 m); the coarse frequency, with a 1000 m unit, gives 423.1 m and so fixes the whole number of 10 m units at 42. Together they give 423.070 m, which the prism constant and the vertical angle turn into 422.460 m horizontal.

spec.aria: An EDM sending a wave to a prism and receiving it back, a ruler of 10 metre units with 42 whole units and a part unit of 3.07 metres, and the coarse and fine readings that give 423.070 metres.

examples.question: An EDM has accuracy ±(3 mm + 3 ppm). It measures a slope distance of 850.000 m. Find the expected error and express the distance with its uncertainty.
steps: Write the distance in km and in mm: 850.000 m = 0.850 km = 850000 mm.
Find the distance-dependent part in mm: b × d = 3 ppm × 0.850 km = 3 × 0.850 = 2.55 mm. Equivalently, 3×10⁻⁶ × 850000 mm = 2.55 mm.
The constant part is a = 3 mm.
Add the two parts: total error = 3 mm + 2.55 mm = 5.55 mm, quoted as 5.6 mm.
Convert to metres for the uncertainty: 5.55 mm = 0.00555 m ≈ 0.006 m.
examples.answer: The distance part is 2.55 mm and the total expected error is 5.55 mm, quoted as 5.6 mm. The distance is 850.000 m ± 0.006 m.
examples.check:
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP
constant_mm = 3.0
ppm = 3.0
distance_m = 850.000
distance_part_mm = ppm * 1e-6 * distance_m * 1000
total_mm = constant_mm + distance_part_mm
rounded_mm = Decimal(str(total_mm)).quantize(Decimal('0.1'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
uncertainty_m = (Decimal(str(total_mm)) / Decimal('1000')).quantize(Decimal('0.001'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
print(f'{distance_part_mm:.2f}')
print(f'{total_mm:.2f}')
print(f'{rounded_mm}')
print(f'{uncertainty_m}')

examples.question: A phase EDM measures with two modulation frequencies. The coarse one has λ/2 = 1000 m and gives a phase difference of 152.3°; the fine one has λ/2 = 10 m and gives 110.52°. (a) Find the distance. (b) The prism constant of −30 mm was not entered; correct the distance. (c) The vertical angle to the prism is +3°00′. Find the horizontal distance.
steps: Coarse distance: 1000 × 152.3/360 = 1000 × 0.4231 = 423.1 m. It is good only to about a metre, but it has no ambiguity within 1000 m.
Fine fraction: 110.52/360 = 0.3070, so the fine reading is 10 × 0.3070 = 3.070 m past a whole number of 10 m units.
Whole number of fine units: N = (423.1 − 3.07)/10 = 42.0, so N = 42.
Prism constant: add −0.030 m, so the slope distance is 423.070 − 0.030 = 423.040 m.
examples.answer: The slope distance is 423.070 m as read, 423.040 m after the prism constant, and the horizontal distance is 422.460 m.

traps: ppm is parts per million, not millimetres per metre. 3 ppm is 3 mm per km, not 3 mm per m.
Add the constant part and the ppm part after scaling. Do not multiply 3 ppm by the constant 3 mm.
The prism constant has a sign and differs by prism type. A wrong value shifts every distance by the same amount.
EDM measures slope distance. Without a vertical angle reduction it is not horizontal distance.
Reflectorless mode is short-range and surface-dependent; it does not remove atmospheric correction or give the same accuracy as a prism.

quiz.q: In an EDM accuracy of ±(3 mm + 3 ppm), what does 3 ppm mean?
quiz.a: 3 parts per million of the measured distance. It equals 3 mm per km.

quiz.q: Why does a phase EDM use two or more modulation frequencies?
quiz.a: One frequency gives only the fractional phase. Multiple frequencies resolve the whole-cycle ambiguity N and provide a coarse and a fine distance.

quiz.q: An EDM has accuracy ±(2 mm + 2 ppm) and measures 1.250 km. Compute the expected error.
quiz.a: ppm part = 2 × 1.250 = 2.5 mm. Total = 2 mm + 2.5 mm = 4.5 mm.

quiz.q: A line is 5 mm too long at 50 m and also 5 mm too long at 500 m. Which error is likely, and why?
quiz.a: A constant additive error such as a wrong prism constant or zero error. An atmospheric ppm error would grow with distance, not stay fixed.

quiz.q: Why are a thermometer and a barometer used with an EDM?
quiz.a: The wave speed in air depends on temperature and pressure. The readings allow the instrument to apply an atmospheric correction in ppm.

quiz.q: Give one practical difference between prism EDM and reflectorless EDM.
quiz.a: A prism returns a strong parallel signal for longer range and has a fixed prism constant. Reflectorless EDM uses surface reflection, has shorter range, depends on the surface and uses no prism constant.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern total stations combine EDM with electronic angle reading and onboard storage; laser scanners and LiDAR use the same time-of-flight or phase idea to measure millions of points. Research improves reflectorless range on dark or wet surfaces and reduces cyclic error. Search for phase-shift EDM, prism constant, atmospheric correction for EDM, and reflectorless total station.
